items.t: 디에스앤지, 차세대 AI 데이터센터 구축 전략 제시…글로벌 기술 협력 강화
items.d: 인공지능(AI) 인프라 전문기업 디에스앤지가 글로벌 기술기업과 함께 차세대 AI 데이터센터 구축을 위한 고밀도 컴퓨팅과 액체 냉각, 데이터 인프라 최적화 전략을 제시했다. 디에스앤지(대표 서정열)는 25일 서울 콘래드 호텔에서 슈퍼마이크로, 엔비디아, DDN 등 글로벌 파트너사가 참여한 가운데 '디에스앤지 이노베이션데이 2026(DS&G Innovation Day 2026)'을 개최했다고 밝혔다. 이번 행사는 AI 데이터센터의 대형화와 고밀도화
items.fullText: 통신 통신 디에스앤지, 차세대 AI 데이터센터 구축 전략 제시…글로벌 기술 협력 강화 발행일 : 2026-11-27 09:02 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 ‘이노베이션데이 2026’ 개최…슈퍼마이크로·엔비디아·DDN 최신 기술 공유 베라 루빈 기반 랙 스케일 컴퓨팅·액체 냉각·데이터 인프라 최적화 방안 발표 AI 인프라 설계부터 구축·운영까지 통합 컨설팅 역량 강화…차세대 서버 전시 인공지능(AI) 인프라 전문기업 디에스앤지가 글로벌 기술기업과 함께 차세대 AI 데이터센터 구축을 위한 고밀도 컴퓨팅과 액체 냉각, 데이터 인프라 최적화 전략을 제시했다. 디에스앤지(대표 서정열)는 25일 서울 콘래드 호텔에서 슈퍼마이크로, 엔비디아, DDN 등 글로벌 파트너사가 참여한 가운데 '디에스앤지 이노베이션데이 2026(DS&G Innovation Day 2026)'을 개최했다고 밝혔다. 이번 행사는 AI 데이터센터의 대형화와 고밀도화에 대응하기 위한 기술 동향을 공유하고 실제 기업 환경에서 적용할 수 있는 인프라 구축·운영 전략을 논의하기 위해 마련됐다. 특히 AI 컴퓨팅 성능뿐 아니라 전력 공급과 냉각 효율, 데이터 처리 성능, 운영비용 등을 종합적으로 고려한 데이터센터 설계 방안이 주요 의제로 다뤄졌다. 슈퍼마이크로는 차세대 AI 컴퓨팅 플랫폼인 엔비디아 베라 루빈(Vera Rubin)을 기반으로 고밀도 AI 인프라 구축 방안을 발표했다. 필립 셔(Philip Sheu) 슈퍼마이크로 GPU 시스템 수석 프로덕트 매니저는 베라 루빈 NVL72와 HGX 루빈 기반 랙 스케일(Rack-Scale) 컴퓨팅 솔루션을 소개했다. AI 인프라 구축 단위가 개별 서버에서 랙과 클러스터로 확대되는 추세에 맞춰 액체 냉각 설계와 케이블리스 구조, 컴퓨팅·스토리지·네트워크 통합 아키텍처를 설명했다. 잭 셰(Jack Hsieh) 슈퍼마이크로 액체 냉각 솔루션 수석 프로덕트 매니저는 데이터센터 빌딩 블록 솔루션(DCBBS)을 기반으로 서버부터 데이터센터 시설 전체에 이르는 통합 냉각 전략을 제시했다. 냉각수 분배 장치(CDU)와 사이드카, 후면 도어 열교환기(RDHx) 등 다양한 냉각 기술을 소개하고 기존 공랭식 데이터센터에 고밀도 AI 시스템을 도입할 때 고려해야 할 시설 요건을 설명했다. 아키라 사노(Akira Sano) 슈퍼마이크로 제너럴 매니저는 최근 열린 고성능 컴퓨팅 국제회의 'SC26'에서 공개된 기술과 글로벌 AI 기업·연구기관의 데이터센터 구축 사례를 공유했다. 엔비디아는 차세대 AI 플랫폼의 시스템 아키텍처를 소개했다. 신민수 엔비디아 이사는 '엔비디아 베라 루빈 레퍼런스 아키텍처'를 주제로 베라 중앙처리장치(CPU)와 루빈 그래픽처리장치(GPU), 고속 네트워크, 데이터 처리 기술을 결합한 시스템 설계 방향을 설명했다. 대규모 AI 모델 학습과 추론 환경에서 개별 GPU 성능뿐 아니라 시스템 전체의 연결성과 확장성이 중요해지고 있다는 점을 강조했다. DDN은 AI 데이터 처리 과정에서 발생하는 병목현상 해소 방안을 제시했다. 김수현 DDN 상무는 '데이터 관리 최적화를 통한 AI 가속화 전략' 발표에서 GPU 성능을 충분히 활용하려면 고성능 스토리지와 효율적인 데이터 관리체계가 뒷받침돼야 한다고 설명했다. 디에스앤지도 자체 기술 역량과 AI 인프라 사업 전략을 공개했다. 최효진 디에스앤지 상무는 '차세대 AI 인프라 기술 동향'을 주제로 컴퓨팅과 네트워크, 메모리, 키·값 캐시(KV Cache), 오케스트레이션, 전력·냉각 기술의 발전 방향을 소개했다. 특히 AI 워크로드가 학습 중심에서 추론으로 확대되는 흐름에 맞춰 코패키지드 광학(CPO) 기반 고속 네트워크와 KV 캐시 최적화, GPU 자원 관리, 800V 직류(DC) 배전 등 차세대 데이터센터 핵심 기술을 설명했다. 서영민 디에스앤지 전무는 글로벌 파트너사의 기술을 실제 고객 환경에 적용하기 위한 통합 컨설팅 전략을 발표했다. 디에스앤지는 GPU 서버와 스토리지

items.t: 엔비디아 칩 판매사, AI 클라우드에 “중국 기업 임대 시 칩 안 판다” 통보
items.d: 엔비디아의 인공지능(AI) 칩을 유통하는 판매업체들이 이른바 '네오클라우드(AI 특화 클라우드)' 기업들을 대상으로 중국 기업에 연산 용량을 일부라도 임대할 경우 칩 공급을 중단하겠다고 통보한 것으로 전해졌다. 26일(현지시간) 미국 CNBC는 엔비디아 칩 판매업체들이 네오클라우드 고객사들에 “중국 기업이 연산 용량을 일부라도(any) 임대하는 구조라면 엔비디아 칩을 구매할 수 없다”는 조건을 전달했다고 보도했다. 구체적인 서버 제조사나 유통사
items.fullText: 반도체 소부장 엔비디아 칩 판매사, AI 클라우드에 “중국 기업 임대 시 칩 안 판다” 통보 발행일 : 2026-11-27 08:33 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 생성형AI 이미지 엔비디아의 인공지능(AI) 칩을 유통하는 판매업체들이 이른바 '네오클라우드(AI 특화 클라우드)' 기업들을 대상으로 중국 기업에 연산 용량을 일부라도 임대할 경우 칩 공급을 중단하겠다고 통보한 것으로 전해졌다. 26일(현지시간) 미국 CNBC는 엔비디아 칩 판매업체들이 네오클라우드 고객사들에 “중국 기업이 연산 용량을 일부라도(any) 임대하는 구조라면 엔비디아 칩을 구매할 수 없다”는 조건을 전달했다고 보도했다. 구체적인 서버 제조사나 유통사 실명은 공개되지 않았으며, 판매업체들이 독자적으로 내건 상업적 거래 조건이라는 설명이다. 이번 조치는 최근 강화된 미국 정부의 공식 수출통제나 엔비디아의 기존 방침보다 훨씬 보수적인 기준이다. 앞서 미 상무부 산업안보국(BIS)은 지난 16일 발표해 19일 발효한 임시최종규칙(IFR)을 통해 중국·마카오 본사 기업에 총처리성능(TPP) 1200만 초과 연산력을 제공할 경우 수출 허가를 받도록 의무화했다. 엔비디아 역시 자체 지침으로 전체 GPU 연산 용량의 50% 이상을 중국 기업에 임대하는 클라우드 업체에 칩 판매를 중단해 왔다. 판매업체들은 이보다 한발 더 나아가 중국 임차인을 아예 배제하는 조건을 내건 셈이다. 유통망이 이처럼 강경한 선제 대응에 나선 배경에는 미국 내 추가 규제 리스크와 금융권의 심사 강화가 맞물려 있다. 제이미슨 그리어 미 무역대표부(USTR) 대표는 동남아 등을 경유한 AI 칩 밀반입과 원격접속 우회 차단을 공언한 상태다. 여기에 해외 데이터센터 원격접속을 직접 통제할 법적 권한을 부여하는 '원격접속보안법(RASA)'이 미 하원을 통과해 상원에 계류 중이어서, 향후 법안 통과 시 유통사까지 제재 위험에 노출될 수 있다는 우려가 커지고 있다. 씨티그룹과 스탠다드차타드 등 글로벌 주요 은행들 역시 동남아 데이터센터 관련 대출 심사를 강화하는 추세다. 이 같은 흐름은 실제 AI 칩 시장의 수급 재배치로 직결되고 있다. CNBC는 전날인 25일에도 소식통 3명을 인용해 BIS 규칙 발효 직후 중국 기업 임대용 데이터센터로 향할 예정이던 엔비디아 'B300' 등 최신 GPU 물량이 갈 곳을 잃어 판매업체들이 새 구매자를 찾고 있다고 전했다. 한편 BIS가 발효한 이번 규칙은 해외 데이터센터 원격접속 자체를 전면 금지하는 것이 아니라 일정 기준 초과 시 및 동남아 등 5개국 행선지에 대해 허가를 의무화하는 조치로, 기존 서비스에 대해서는 2027년 2월 17일까지 90일간의 유예 기간이 부여됐다. 다만 공식 규제의 유예 기간과 무관하게 칩 유통망과 금융권이 선제적으로 중국 자본·기업과의 거래 단절에 나서면서, 글로벌 네오클라우드 업계의 고객사 재편과 유휴 GPU 물량 이동은 당분간 이어질 전망이다. 이형두 기자 dudu@etnews.com

items.t: “트럼프, 주가 오르면 내 덕분, 내리면 남 탓”-NYT
items.d: 도널드 트럼프 미 대통령은 줄곧 주가가 오르면 내 덕분이고 주가가 하락하면 남 탓을 해왔다고 미 뉴욕타임스(NYT)가 지난 25일(현지시각) 보도했다. 트럼프는 엔비디아 이사회를 설득해 젠슨 황을 최고경영자로 복귀시킨 뒤 엔비디아 주가가 30% 넘게 급등하자 신이 나서 “이제 올바른 방향으로 치솟는 로켓이 됐다”고 외쳤다. 그러나 엔비디아 주가는 24일 5.9% 하락한 데 이어 25일에도 5% 떨어졌다. 이는 투자자들이 황의 사임과 복귀, 인공지능 거품이 엔비디아의 장기 주가 전망에 부담이 된다고 판단하고 있음을 시사한다. 또 이란 전쟁과 관세 인상 등 트럼프의 여러 조치도 주가 하락에 영향을 미쳤을 것이다. 트럼프는 주가 상승을 자신이 경제 운영을 잘하는 증거로 내세워 오면서도 주가 하락에도 대통령이 책임

items.d: 엔비디아가 인공지능(AI) 칩에 대한 중국의 우회 접근을 막으려는 미국 정부의 새 수출 통제 조치에 대응해 동남아시아 주요국으로 향하는 AI 서버 출하를 중단했다. 영국 파이낸셜타임스(FT)는 26일(현지시간) 엔비디아가 델과 슈퍼마이크로 등 주요 서버 제조 협력사에 말레이시아·싱가포르·태국·인도네시아 등 4개국행 AI 서버 선적을 중단하라고 지시했다고 보도했다. 이들 협력사는 최근 현지 고객사들에 “엔비디아가 주문 물량의 출하를 허용하지 않고
items.fullText: 반도체 반도체 엔비디아, 동남아 4개국 AI 서버 출하 중단…美 '中 우회 접근' 차단 여파 발행일 : 2026-11-27 08:07 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 엔비디아가 인공지능(AI) 칩에 대한 중국의 우회 접근을 막으려는 미국 정부의 새 수출 통제 조치에 대응해 동남아시아 주요국으로 향하는 AI 서버 출하를 중단했다. 영국 파이낸셜타임스(FT)는 26일(현지시간) 엔비디아가 델과 슈퍼마이크로 등 주요 서버 제조 협력사에 말레이시아·싱가포르·태국·인도네시아 등 4개국행 AI 서버 선적을 중단하라고 지시했다고 보도했다. 이들 협력사는 최근 현지 고객사들에 “엔비디아가 주문 물량의 출하를 허용하지 않고 있다”고 통보한 것으로 전해졌다. 이번 조치는 미국 상무부가 지난 19일 시행한 강화된 AI 칩 수출 통제 규정에 따른 것이다. 그동안 중국 AI 개발사들은 미국의 직접 수출 규제를 피하기 위해 동남아 4개국에 구축된 현지 클라우드 기업의 데이터센터 컴퓨팅 자원을 임대하는 방식으로 엔비디아 칩을 활용해 왔다. 미 상무부의 새 규제는 이들 4개국(및 브라질)으로 수출되는 첨단 AI 칩에 별도 허가를 의무화하고, 클라우드 사업자가 90일 이내에 최종 사용자 중 제재 대상 기관이 없음을 입증하도록 하는 내용을 담고 있다. 엔비디아와 파트너사들은 현재 미 당국의 규정을 준수할 방안을 모색 중이며, 이번 출하 중단이 일시적일지 장기화될지는 불투명한 상태다. 현지 클라우드 업계 관계자는 FT에 “90일의 허가 기한이 흘러가고 있지만 구체적인 신청 가이드라인조차 없어 현장에 극심한 혼란이 빚어지고 있다”고 전했다. 엔비디아는 이와 관련한 논평을 거부했다. 출하 중단 여파는 중국 빅테크 수요를 바탕으로 급성장해 온 동남아 데이터센터 산업과 금융권으로 즉각 번지고 있다. FT에 따르면 싱가포르 기반 클라우드 기업 아올라니는 말레이시아에서 틱톡 모회사 바이트댄스에 AI 컴퓨팅 파워를 공급할 예정이었으나, 이번 조치로 일부 은행들이 약 5억달러(약 7000억원) 규모의 대출 집행을 보류했다. 바이트댄스 역시 해당 계약을 파기할 가능성이 제기되고 있다. 이번 규제는 엔비디아 실적에도 적지 않은 부담으로 작용할 전망이다. FT가 인용한 기업 공시에 따르면, 엔비디아의 지난해 싱가포르 법인 매출(대만·중국 일부 매출 포함)은 전년 대비 72% 급증한 1040억달러(약 145조원)에 달해 매출 비중이 큰 핵심 거점으로 꼽혀왔다. 이형두 기자 dudu@etnews.com

items.t: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, saying he went ‘too far’ and is in therapy
items.d: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Jensen Huang says he’s thankful for second chance at Nvidia employee meeting The CEO acknowledged that he had gone ‘too far’ with some of his workplace behavior and said he has been going to therapy every day, a source told NBC News. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Tech stocks take a dip as Jensen Huang comes back as Nvidia CEO 04:53 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 11:11 PM EST By Jean Lee and Jared Perlo Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around. No company has impacted the world as deeply or profoundly as Nvidia, Huang said, according to an Nvidia employee who attended the meeting. Huang called the company’s story the most interesting in the world. According to the individual, Huang expressed contrition for his past behavior and was adamant that employees should follow the company’s code of conduct. The AI hardware leader resigned from the company Nov. 12 amid mounting scrutiny about alleged romantic relationships with subordinates and Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed. According to U.S. intelligence officials, Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. He also said that he has been regularly attending therapy and that he had been deeply embarrassed about recent events, the source said. The CEO was met with an overwhelmingly positive reception, even receiving a standing ovation, according to the source. Huang’s return marked a nearly unprecedented case of corporate whiplash. items.t: Trump says pardon is always an option for Huang, and that invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary
items.d: The president’s assertion that Huang does not pose a national security threat has sparked bipartisan backlash on Capitol Hill, where the Nvidia CEO is set to testify next week.
items.fullText: Donald Trump Trump says pardon is always an option for Jensen Huang, and that invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary The president’s assertion that Huang does not pose a national security threat has drawn skepticism on Capitol Hill, where the Nvidia CEO is set to testify next week. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 President Donald Trump presents the National Medal of Science to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in Washington on Oct. 8. Kent Nishimura / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 9:19 PM EST By Kyla Guilfoil President Donald Trump said that while pardoning Jensen Huang for any potential criminal activity remains an option, he doesn’t think that will be needed for the newly reinstated Nvidia CEO . “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” Trump told the New York Post in an interview published Tuesday night. Asked about Huang’s scheduled appearances next week on Capitol Hill, Trump said, “I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people.” “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person,” the president said. A representative for Huang declined to comment on Trump’s comments. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for further comment. Speaking at a news conference Tuesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche indicated he would have told Trump if Huang had been involved in any criminal activity. “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. items.t: Blanche calls Nvidia a ‘good corporate citizen’ while dodging questions on probe

items.fullText: Trump administration Todd Blanche calls Nvidia a ‘good corporate citizen’ while dodging questions on investigation President Donald Trump had said the Justice Department had “exonerated” the chip giant’s newly reinstated CEO, Jensen Huang. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Blanche says he would have told Trump about any crimes Jensen Huang committed 01:22 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 1:37 PM EST By Dareh Gregorian and Helen Graham Attorney General Todd Blanche on Tuesday praised Nvidia as a “good corporate citizen” while sidestepping questions about the Justice Department’s role in the president’s controversial decision to push for the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he’d spoken to Blanche and “they did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he himself was exonerated,” referring to Huang. Asked at an unrelated press conference about Trump’s remarks, Blanche said, “What the president said is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him,” before adding, “I’m not going to get into communications I have with the president about it.” He then said that what Trump was saying “is exactly right.” “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. NBC News previously reported that Trump sought Blanche and Vice President JD Vance’s help in convincing Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back. An administration official said the attorney general told the president that the DOJ had no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang or the company. items.fullText: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs NVIDIA and Microsoft expand tools for enterprises to customize AI models and deploy applications across cloud and local infrastructure. November 19, 2026 by Dave Salvator 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs. At Microsoft Ignite , the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to NVIDIA open models and customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry, and new options for running AI at the edge, where businesses generate and use their data. Microsoft is also using NVIDIA technologies to accelerate its own models and services, including NVIDIA Dynamo inference software for post-training and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Bing search models. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Running in Azure NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are running in Azure data centers , providing infrastructure designed for demanding reasoning, agentic applications, and large-scale model training and inference. Microsoft and NVIDIA are also collaborating to extend confidential computing to bare-metal and rack-scale AI infrastructure. The work will help protect sensitive models and data while they are being processed, supporting organizations that need to work with proprietary or regulated information. NVIDIA Confidential Computing and attestation help customers verify the computing environment before releasing sensitive models, data or keys. As AI workloads span more interconnected accelerators, the companies are working to extend those protections across the AI factory infrastructure. items.fullText: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now Systems from ASUS, Dell and MSI are now available — with more from Acer, GIGABYTE, HP and Microsoft on the way — bringing RTX acceleration and up to 128GB of unified memory to local AI, development and creative workflows. November 18, 2026 by Justin Walker 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. items.fullText: NVIDIA DGX Spark Developer Kit Turns a Desk Into a Supercomputing Lab Build and test scientific applications by connecting up to four NVIDIA DGX Spark systems for a combined 512GB of shared memory, without waiting for a spot on shared systems. November 16, 2026 by Allen Bourgoyne 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. A Supercomputing Lab on Any Desk The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 16TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. items.fullText: How the World’s Most Advanced AI Infrastructure Supply Chain Invents the Future Over two decades running the most complex manufacturing on the planet, NVIDIA operations chief Deb Shoquist has required three things of every supply chain partner: extreme technical skill, unshakeable trust and a willingness to always try something new. November 16, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. items.fullText: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics November 16, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.” Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Quantum hardware developers, software providers and supercomputing centers are adopting the community-built Slurm workloads manager and the NVIDIA quantum platform to integrate quantum processors, design future systems and develop scientific applications. November 16, 2026 by Sam Stanwyck 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Beating the Bottleneck Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. items.fullText: NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training and Endpoints as Vera Rubin Debuts With Leading Performance November 16, 2026 by Shruti Koparkar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! In its MLPerf benchmarks debut, with results released today, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform delivers leading performance across training, post-training and agentic inference. NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and, in its first MLPerf Endpoints submission, delivered more than 10x generational gains in throughput per watt for agentic AI — measuring how much agentic work a system delivers with each watt of power. These results are just the beginning. Vera Rubin performance will keep climbing through continuous optimization of NVIDIA’s CUDA-powered software stack , so the infrastructure that customers invest in today delivers more value over time. NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training v6.1 AI agents are now everywhere, writing code, running business workflows, answering customer questions and, as this week’s SC26 conference highlights , advancing scientific research. Faster training means smarter agents can reach users sooner, drug discovery models can keep pace with new lab data and fraud-detection models can adapt to new threats faster. MLPerf Training measures how fast a system can train a range of AI models to a target level of accuracy. The NVIDIA platform was the only one with results on every benchmark this round, spanning large language models, image generation, recommender systems and reinforcement learning post-training. In its debut, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 2x more performance per GPU than the highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 system — early results that show the pace of generation-over-generation innovation. items.fullText: NVIDIA CUDA-X Libraries Give Agents the Tools to Accelerate Scientific Discovery November 16, 2026 by Kibibi Moseley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. Steering Fusion Simulations Sustaining plasma at millions of degrees is essential to achieving stable, continuous fusion energy. But simulating its behavior is costly: on petascale systems, a single time step can take days, with simulations running for weeks.
